title: ～たて — “freshly ～ed / just done”
summary: The suffix たて attaches to the stem (masu-stem) of a verb and means “just finished being ～ed, fresh.” It describes things that are in the best, newest state, like freshly baked bread. It is used mainly with food and new items.

patterns.form: 動詞ます形の語幹 ＋ たて
patterns.gloss: masu-stem + たて (焼きたて, 出来たて, とれたて)

body.p: Drop ます from the verb and add たて: 焼く → 焼きたて, 取れる → とれたて, 出来る → 出来たて. The result works like a noun and can describe another noun with の: 焼きたてのパン.

It is fixed in a limited set of words: 焼きたて (freshly baked), 炊きたて (freshly cooked rice), 出来たて (just made), とれたて (freshly picked/caught), 生まれたて (newborn), 洗いたて (freshly washed). Do not make it freely with any verb.
～たばかり just says an action finished a short time ago. ～たて carries the positive feeling that the thing is still fresh and at its best.

examples.ja: 焼（や）きたてのパンはとてもおいしい。
examples.romaji: Yakitate no pan wa totemo oishii.
examples.tr: Freshly baked bread is very delicious.

examples.ja: とれたての野菜（やさい）は、味（あじ）が濃（こ）くておいしい。
examples.romaji: Toretate no yasai wa, aji ga kute oishii.
examples.tr: Freshly picked vegetables taste rich and delicious.

examples.ja: 出来（でき）たての料理（りょうり）を、熱（あつ）いうちにどうぞ。
examples.romaji: Dekitate no ryōri o, atsui uchi ni dōzo.
examples.tr: Please enjoy the freshly made dish while it's still hot.

pitfalls: Attach it to the masu-stem, not to the ta-form: 焼きたて, not 焼いたたて.
It is a limited set of words. For other actions, use ～たばかり.
